_comment: What grows in the Meadows playground, and where. ALL of it is TUNABLE. The expected feedback is 'too sparse', 'too busy', 'the trees are on the cliffs' — every one of those has to be answerable here rather than in a scene.
_comment_authored: This dresses the M1 MOVEMENT PLAYGROUND, not the real Meadows. M7 authors the actual geography and its placement will be authored rather than scattered. The RULES survive that; the specific clump centres do not.
_comment_clumping: Every layer clusters. Evenly-spread props at uniform scale are the readable signature of generator output — the visual rubric names it — so each layer places clumps and scatters within them, leaving clearings between. `strays` fills the gaps so the clumps do not read as islands.
_comment_pack: Quaternius Stylized Nature MegaKit (CC0), replacing Kenney's Nature Kit. The blind critic's verdict on the Kenney set was that every tree was the same tree — 'one straight tapered trunk, one 6-8 face canopy, two greens, varied only by uniform scale' — and that the far tree line read as 'a row of identical cards at near-uniform spacing along a contour: a fence of icons'. It measured mid-distance trees at 1.00:1 luminance contrast against the ground behind them, meaning invisible. This pack ships four genuinely different tree species with real bark and leaf TEXTURES and normal maps, which is what that complaint was actually about.
_comment_scale: These models are authored in METRES, unlike Kenney's which were about one unit tall and needed a 3.4x per-layer correction. So `base_scale` is near 1.0 here and mostly trims rather than multiplies. Measured with tools/measure_models.gd rather than guessed — guessing produced a meadow of knee-high trees once already.
_comment_ev2: EV2 (bible sec10): an APPROVED SUBSET, not all 116 models in the fuller pack. `trees` (standard canopy) and `grove` (hero trees) are each cut to the bible's counts and given controlled spring/deep/yellow-green variants per model instead of one flat colour; `saplings` is new. Two of the bible's asks are NOT done here and are recorded rather than faked: 'wetland forms near river' was blocked on there being no water at all; EV5 has since shipped the pond/stream and reed stands at the banks, but a dedicated wetland MESH still does not exist; and the rock family's '2-3 large' tier has no distinct large-format mesh in the imported subset (the fuller Stylized Nature MegaKit is itch.io-blocked, see EV1-remainder in BLOCKED.md) — reusing the existing Rock_Medium meshes in a second layer would silently break their tint/collision via vegetation.gd's known models-shared-across-layers failure mode, so the existing single `rocks` layer's 0.28-2.1 scale span (already producing large-boulder reads from the same 3 medium meshes) stands as the honest ceiling until more geometry is unblocked.

trees._comment: The common broadleaf, 7-9m. The everyday tree of the meadow, in copses.
trees._comment_ev2: EV2 (bible sec10): 'standard canopy' wants 3-4 medium forms, not all 5. Measured with tools/measure_models.gd rather than guessed: kept the 3 forms with the widest canopy footprint (CommonTree_1 19.7sq.m, _2 19.1, _3 17.2 -- the bar this item is judged against is 'reads as one species family at thumbnail size', which is a footprint/silhouette question, not a triangle-count one). CommonTree_4 and _5 (14.4 and 15.5sq.m, the narrowest two) move to the new `saplings` layer below at reduced scale -- same species, a young form -- rather than being dropped outright.
trees._comment_seed_offset_of12r: OF12-remainder: this layer's own RNG stream re-rolled in place (scatter_rules.gd::all_placements). The unbiased scatter happened to put a 3-tree stand and a 4-tree stand at nearly matched heights/along-path distance on opposite sides of The Rise route's first leg -- named by all three of OF12's blind critics as reading like an authored gateway framing the path, which no anchor or design intent put there. `1` was the smallest offset tried that breaks the near-side count match (probed headlessly with tools/_probe_rise_trees.gd before rendering) without reshuffling the rest of the map's already-tuned trees (a top-level `seed` bump would have). TUNABLE.
trees._comment_clumping: Fewer, tighter, larger copses rather than more small ones. 26 clumps of 9 spread over 512m is close enough to even that it reads as a distribution; twelve dense copses with real gaps between them reads as somebody deciding where a wood goes.
trees._comment_ridge_bias: R7.1-remainder: specific sightlines toward the true horizon (the last real hilltops before Terrain3D's own procedural background takes over past the 512m bake) could still land on a gap between clumps, even though far clumps exist elsewhere. ridge_bias makes half this layer's clumps sample several candidate centres and keep the highest, biasing toward hilltops/ridge crests without hand-picked coordinates (scatter_rules.gd). Not a density increase — same clump count, biased placement. Tune by rendering, not by feel.
trees._comment_slope: Trees stop well before the rocky rises. A tree growing out of a cliff face is the cheapest way to destroy the sense that a place was authored.
trees._comment_min_height_ev5: EV5: keep out of the pond. Only the pond basin is below -18m anywhere on the map, so a min_height gate is exactly a waterline rule (water level -22.5, terrain_playground.json). Trees stop 0.9m of elevation above the waterline, clear of the damp shore ring. TUNABLE.
trees._comment_scale: A 2.5x spread inside one copse. Uniform prop scale is one of the two readable signatures of generator output, and a wood with saplings and old trees in it is the difference between a grove and a stamp.
trees._comment_clear: The spawn pad stays clear. The player's first sight of the game should not be the inside of a tree.
trees._comment_harvest_r2_3: R2.3: the world's own scattered trees, not a second set of authored nodes on top of them -- makes the biggest single ground-cover layer double as the wood supply once harvest_node.gd's ~10 tutorial spots stop being enough. 1-in-12 (0.083) of ~230 trees is ~19 real gather points, spread evenly through the layer's own draw order (scatter_rules.gd) rather than clustered by chance. TUNABLE.
trees._comment_leaf: R9.4. Leaves_NormalTree_C.png measures RGB(88,123,0) -- saturation 1.00, the maximum a colour can have, at hue 77, which is the same chartreuse the ground already is. The blind critic measured 91% of every saturated pixel in frames 01 and 04 inside one 30-degree hue bin and called the world monochromatic; the canopy was reinforcing the ground rather than contrasting with it. Leaves.png is the same pack's muted leaf -- RGB(114,131,50), saturation 0.62 -- and the retint warms it one step further off the grass hue. Same mechanism the bushes layer has used since the crimson-bush fix. No new asset. TUNABLE. R9.4 round 2: the retint now aims at palette.json's meadow.leaf_green_deep (#496c34, hue 98) rather than at a warm cream. Round 1 swapped the texture and stopped the canopy being the MOST saturated thing in frame, but left it at hue ~70 -- the same family as the ground, so frame_stats still measured 85-89% of chromatic pixels in one hue bin against the references' three to five. A canopy has to be a different green from the grass under it, not a brighter one.
trees._comment_leaf_magenta_fix: Backlog item 'A near-field tree renders with magenta/red-striped foliage', found in `dome-overview.png`/`road-end-lookup.png`. R9.4's own description of Leaves.png as a single 'muted leaf' colour was wrong: it is a MULTI-SPECIES SAMPLE SHEET -- green, blue, orange and a saturated magenta/pink leaf pair (measured RGB(216,55,135), full alpha) all on one 512x512 canvas. CommonTree's leaf cards are alpha-cutout billboards that each sample nearly the FULL 0-1 UV square (measured directly: median per-triangle UV bounding box 0.80x1.00 on CommonTree_1's canopy primitive), the same technique Leaves_NormalTree_C.png's own single-hue 'flower of leaflets' layout was built for. Pointed at Leaves.png instead, every card renders ALL of the atlas's leaf shapes at once, in their true colours -- confirmed with an isolated close-up repro (single tree, no terrain, no distance blending) that shows green, teal, orange AND magenta/crimson shards on one canopy. Reverted the swap target back to Leaves_NormalTree_C.png -- already proven safe as the `bushes` layer's own crimson-bush fix -- which removes the contamination entirely. Traded off: the round-2 desaturation this comment describes relied on Leaves.png's nonzero blue channel (texture*tint can only ever REDUCE saturation, never below what the base texture's own minimum channel allows, and Leaves_NormalTree_C.png's blue channel is 0 -- pinned at max saturation regardless of tint). The 3-step variant_retint hue spread below (94/97/81 degrees post-multiply) still applies and still gives CommonTree three distinguishable greens; only the saturation reduction R9.4 round 1 bought is given back. Not re-litigated here -- flagged honestly, not silently reintroduced.
trees._comment_variant: EV2: 'controlled material variants -- spring, deep and yellow-green -- not a different colour per tree' (bible sec10). Three fixed steps, one per remaining model, not per-instance jitter. Round 1 of EV2's own blind pass tried R9.4's shipped #9dcaff (`spring`) plus a straight darken (`deep`) -- both BLUE-hued multiplies (hue ~213) that land in the intended green family on Leaves.png's dark/average texels but multiply through nearly unchanged on bright highlight texels, reading as cyan/teal flecks a blind critic named directly. Round 2 fixed the hue (green-hued multiplies, hue 77-112, confirmed fleck-free by an independent second blind pass) but that pass's own close pixel inspection found the three still clustered in a 63-84 degree rendered hue band -- too narrow to read as distinguishable varieties once scene lighting compresses it further, even though the un-lit albedo maths looked separated. These values push both hue (77/96/103 after the same texture-multiply check) AND value (0.20/0.19/0.09) further apart -- `deep` in particular is now a genuinely darker tint, not just a different hue at the same brightness -- while the highlight-case check (a synthetic near-white texel) still stays inside 75-130 degrees, short of the ~150 degree line where the round-1 cyan artifact started.
trees._comment_anchors_of4_mound: OF4-remainder-mound. A BROKEN tree line along the rise's village-facing foot, and a few trees standing on the lower flank. A 7-9m tree is the cheapest ruler a landform can carry -- with nothing of known size anywhere on it the rise read as 'an enlarged pebble' to a blind critic, which is a scale failure, not a texture one. Slope is relaxed to 25 degrees for these draws only (this layer's own 21-degree ceiling stays as tuned everywhere else) so the line climbs a little way onto the flank instead of stopping dead at the break. Round 2: the three groups were the same size at the same radius and read as 'a ring following the hill's foot contour at near-even spacing' -- now one dense copse, one loose stand and one pair, at three different radii, which is the difference between a wood and a hedge. ALL TUNABLE.

anchors._why: north-west foot: the dense copse
west foot, north of the road terminus: a loose stand
south-west foot: just a pair, so the line is not continuous

grove._comment: The ancient twisted oaks, 15-19m and far broader. A genuinely DIFFERENT species, not the same mesh retinted — which was the previous version of this layer and exactly what the critic caught. These are the landmark trees: at twice the height of a common tree and three times the canopy, a stand of them reads from across the playground.
grove._comment_ev2: EV2 (bible sec10): 'hero trees' wants 2-3 large forms -- 'broad oak, asymmetrical old tree, tall landmark tree' -- not all 5. Measured with tools/measure_models.gd: TwistedTree_1 has the widest footprint (13.52x11.55, the 'broad oak'), TwistedTree_2 is the tallest (18.95m, the 'tall landmark tree'), and TwistedTree_4 is the only one of the five where depth exceeds width (10.38x11.29 -- a genuinely lopsided footprint, the 'asymmetrical old tree'). TwistedTree_3 and _5 read as near-symmetric restatements of _1 and _2 by the same measure and are cut.
grove._comment_ev2_landmark_ceiling: EV2-landmark-ceiling: a blind critic ranked all 3 TwistedTree forms short of the key art's oaks -- 'canopies wider than they are tall, trunks visibly fork and lean' -- and TwistedTree_1 (the 'broad oak' slot, width/height 0.81) was the least-bad, still failing. Measured every tree in the fuller Stylized Nature MegaKit (assets_raw/vendor/quaternius_stylized-nature-megakit/, staged d64df71) by reading each glTF's own POSITION bounds directly: CherryBlossom_3 (16.59w x 14.49h x 13.03d, width/height 1.15) is the ONLY form in the entire pack genuinely wider than tall. Replaces TwistedTree_1 -- not appended as a 4th form -- because ENVIRONMENT_AND_UI_BIBLE.md sec10 caps hero trees at 2-3 forms. Honest limit: no candidate's glTF has separate trunk/branch nodes, so 'visibly forking trunk' isn't confirmed by data alone -- a render/blind-judge question, not yet run.
grove._comment_count: Deliberately few. A 10,000-triangle tree is thirty times a Kenney one, and these are the biggest thing in the world — a stand of six is a landmark, forty is a forest nobody can walk through.
grove._comment_min_height_ev5: EV5: keep out of the pond. Only the pond basin is below -18m anywhere on the map, so a min_height gate is exactly a waterline rule (water level -22.5, terrain_playground.json). Same shoreline standoff as the standard canopy. TUNABLE.
grove._comment_retexture: The pack ships `Leaves_TwistedTree_C` as a CRIMSON autumn leaf. Left alone it made the biggest trees in the meadow blood red and they dominated every frame. Warm hue has to come from the flowers, the dry grass and the golden hour, not from painting the whole canopy.
grove._comment_colour:
These stay CRIMSON, at the owner's call: 'I actually really like the red trees.'

It is also the right call against the review. The critic measured the palette as a single yellow-green wedge — 60-90% of pixels in one hue family in every frame — and said the board's golds and warm ends appear nowhere. A stand of turning oaks is the one thing in the meadow carrying a second hue family at tree height, and it does it with the pack's own authored texture rather than a tint.

Kept DELIBERATELY few for that reason: 6 clumps of 5. Warm accent against green reads as autumn; warm everywhere reads as a different biome. The bushes still get retextured green (they share this material) because 800 red bushes is a carpet, not an accent.
grove._comment_palette: The twisted trees' canopy is CRIMSON (the pack's leaf texture, not a tint). The key art's Meadows is green-oak country with red held back as an accent, and the blind critique called the old mix (38 red trees, clumped near the spawn) 'autumn-danger everywhere' - red is also supposed to be reserved for Team Tether. ~16 spread across the map keeps them as the landmark accent they were meant to be. TUNABLE.
grove._comment_leaf: R9.4. THE RED LEAK, found by two independent blind reviews eleven days apart. Leaves_TwistedTree_C.png is RGB(167,23,23) -- hue 0, saturation 0.86, a crimson autumn leaf -- which made the grove the most saturated warm thing in the whole survey, on decorative trees beside the starting village. docs/reference/README.md and the visual-judge rubric both reserve deep red/oxblood for Team Tether danger, and spending it on scenery leaves the faction nothing to claim. The bushes layer hit this exact texture and fixed it by swapping -- see its retexture block and _retint()'s own comment in vegetation.gd -- the grove was simply never given the same treatment. No multiply turns red into green, so it has to be a swap. TUNABLE. R9.4 round 2: the retint now aims at palette.json's meadow.leaf_green_deep (#496c34, hue 98) rather than at a warm cream. Round 1 swapped the texture and stopped the canopy being the MOST saturated thing in frame, but left it at hue ~70 -- the same family as the ground, so frame_stats still measured 85-89% of chromatic pixels in one hue bin against the references' three to five. A canopy has to be a different green from the grass under it, not a brighter one.
grove._comment_leaf_magenta_fix: Magenta-canopy fix (see `trees` layer's own comment for the full mechanism): Leaves.png is a multi-species sample sheet, not a single muted leaf, and this layer's leaf cards sample nearly the whole canvas the same way CommonTree's do -- so the hero oaks carried the same green/blue/orange/magenta contamination. Swap target changed to Leaves_NormalTree_C.png, matching the `bushes` layer's own already-safe choice for this exact material.
grove._comment_cherryblossom_material: EV2-landmark-ceiling's blind-verify render (a close-up of the shipped CherryBlossom_3 instance, since none of tools/survey.gd's 5 fixed cameras happen to land near a grove clump) found the canopy still rendering its native pink/purple cherry-blossom texture, in the flesh, not swapped -- every retexture/retint/variant_retint key below was `Leaves_TwistedTree`, and CherryBlossom_3.gltf's own leaf material is named `Leaves_CherryBlossom` (checked directly against the glTF JSON), a different string that none of them ever matched. Added alongside, not instead of, the TwistedTree keys -- both models share this layer.
grove._comment_variant: EV2: the same 3-step spring/deep/yellow-green family as the `trees` layer (bible sec10), so the hero trees read as kin to the standard canopy rather than a fourth palette. One variant per remaining model, not per-instance jitter. CherryBlossom_3 takes the `spring` step, the same one TwistedTree_1 carried before EV2-landmark-ceiling replaced it in this species slot.
grove._comment_anchors_of4_mound: OF4-remainder-mound. Two stands of the hero oaks at the rise's foot, at either end of the village-facing arc. These are the tallest things in the game (8-14m placed) and they do what the common canopy cannot: give the base of a 46m landform something with a known height standing against it, so the eye can size the hill from the village square. Kept to two stands -- this layer's whole comment above is about why a landmark tree stops being one when there are forty. ALL TUNABLE.

anchors._why: north-west foot stand
south-west foot stand

saplings._comment: EV2 (bible sec10): 'young/small, 2-3 sapling forms'. No dedicated sapling mesh exists in the imported subset, and the fuller Stylized Nature MegaKit is itch.io-blocked (see EV1-remainder in BLOCKED.md) -- so this reuses CommonTree_4 and _5, the two narrowest standard-canopy forms cut from the `trees` layer above, at young-tree scale instead of medium-tree scale. Same species, a different age, not a new model -- exactly what the bible means by controlled variants rather than clutter.
saplings._comment_no_overlap: CommonTree_4/_5 belong to THIS layer only, not `trees` too -- vegetation.gd groups placements by model path for drawing, so a model listed in two layers silently loses one layer's tint/collision settings (see _warn_about_shared_models). Keeping the two lists disjoint is what avoids that.
saplings._comment_placement: Understory at the edge of the standard-canopy copses -- smaller clumps, tighter radius, no ridge bias -- so a wood reads as having an age range rather than every tree planted the same year.
saplings._comment_min_height_ev5: EV5: keep out of the pond. Only the pond basin is below -18m anywhere on the map, so a min_height gate is exactly a waterline rule (water level -22.5, terrain_playground.json). Same shoreline standoff as the standard canopy. TUNABLE.
saplings._comment_scale: A young CommonTree at roughly a third the height of a mature one -- 2.5-3.5m against the standard canopy's 7-9m -- read against a 1.8m trainer, not guessed.
saplings._comment_leaf_magenta_fix: Same magenta-canopy fix as the `trees` layer above (see its comment for the full mechanism) -- CommonTree_4/_5 share the Leaves_NormalTree material and the same full-canvas leaf-card technique, so they carried the identical green/blue/orange/magenta contamination from Leaves.png.
saplings._comment_variant: The same two non-spring variants as the standard canopy, so the sapling layer reads as the same species at a different age rather than a third palette.

deadfall._comment: Dead trees and mushrooms. The dead trees are 9-13m bare silhouettes and do a job no living tree can: they break a green tree line with a grey vertical, which is most of what stops a treeline reading as a hedge.
deadfall._comment_drain_sd16: D41: a dead tree does not die twice. This layer is the one thing that should INCREASE around a Tether station, so it opts out of the suppression entirely and the quarry gets an authored stand instead (below). `models` on that anchor narrows this layer's list to the three dead trees -- the mushrooms belong under a living canopy, not on drained ground.

anchors._comment_cleared: The quarry's own clearing (below) covers this anchor's whole radius, and a clearing culls every layer that can block sight -- deadfall included -- so without this the stand would be authored and then silently thrown away. An anchor overriding a layer key for its own draws is exactly what anchors are for: the clearing exists to stop the SCATTER growing a copse through a working face, not to veto a hand-placed one.
anchors._why: SD16/D41: the standing dead around the quarry's conduit head. Half the drained-ground read is what is MISSING (the scatter thins itself out); this is the other half, the grey verticals that say something used to grow here.

deadfall._comment_min_height_ev5: EV5: keep out of the pond. Only the pond basin is below -18m anywhere on the map, so a min_height gate is exactly a waterline rule (water level -22.5, terrain_playground.json). A dead tree IN the pond would be a nice touch one day, but placed deliberately, not by a scatter that cannot see the water. TUNABLE.
deadfall._comment_count: R9.4. Was clumps 14 / per_clump 3 / strays 20 -- 62 bare dead trees in the biome the key art board calls 'peaceful by day'. The blind critic called them 'simultaneously the ugliest and the most out-of-palette objects present' and noted they occupy about a third of frame 04 as its compositional foreground: untextured cool grey-violet tubes in a warm-lit green scene. They earn a place as occasional character, not as the meadow's most prominent vertical element. Cut to 18, held further off the village by clear_radius, and warmed out of violet by the retint so they read as weathered wood rather than ash. TUNABLE.

bushes._comment: The middle layer. Without something between grass height and tree height the ground reads as a lawn with poles on it. Ferns and broad plants included, because undergrowth banked at the base of a tree is what makes a copse read as a wood rather than as trees standing on a lawn.
bushes._comment_path_edge_jitter_ev3_remainder_: EV3-remainder-2: see scatter_rules.gd's own comment. Every ground-cover layer shares one path-exclusion isoline, and terrain_playground.json's four routes all meet at the village well -- their combined exclusion wedges read as a converging fan across every layer at once, not a per-layer defect. OF12 widened 0.15 -> 0.35 on the walkthrough ground-cover layers (bushes stay at 0.25 -- a shrub standing in the worn shoulder reads as blocking the road, a tuft reads as encroachment): a blind critic named the dirt/grass boundary 'a clean cut with no interpenetration', and a wider per-instance threshold spread lets the occasional plant stand visibly INTO the fade band. TUNABLE.
bushes._comment_path_standoff_of12: OF12 round 2: bushes gain the same noise-varying standoff as grass so their new verge fringe below is culled stretch-by-stretch too, not strung uniformly. Distinct wavelength/salt from every other layer. TUNABLE.
bushes._comment_verge_of12: OF12 round 2: a few real shrubs in the fringe give it height variety -- a verge of only ankle tufts still reads mown. Deliberately few. TUNABLE.
bushes._comment_min_height_ev5: EV5: keep out of the pond. Only the pond basin is below -18m anywhere on the map, so a min_height gate is exactly a waterline rule (water level -22.5, terrain_playground.json). Bushes reach nearer the waterline than trees but stay dry. TUNABLE.
bushes._comment_retexture: Bush_Common and Bush_Common_Flowers use the material `Leaves_TwistedTree`, whose texture the pack ships CRIMSON — it is the autumn variant of the twisted oak. Unswapped, every bush in the meadow came out blood red, and no colour multiply turns red into green. This points them at the pack's own green leaf instead.

grass._comment: Tufts, not a ground texture. These are what make the terrain read as a meadow rather than as a painted surface, and they are the layer whose density most separates these frames from the reference — Palworld's meadows measure 3-9% featureless ground against this build's 56-66%.
grass._comment_species_of12_b: OF12-remainder (b): grass had exactly one species (a Common Short/Tall pair) despite the layer's own density work above. Grass_Wide_Short/Tall, curated from the fuller Stylized Nature MegaKit (assets_raw/vendor/quaternius_stylized-nature-megakit/, staged d64df71), add a second matched pair with a genuinely broader footprint (1.04-1.16m vs Common's 0.64-0.90m) -- real silhouette variety, not a renamed duplicate. Same Grass/Grass.png material as every other model in this layer, so no new texture or retint plumbing needed; the existing scale_min/scale_max trims both pairs into the same knee-height band uniformly (scatter_rules.gd has no per-model weight/scale field). TUNABLE -- Grass_Wheat was considered and left for drygrass instead, its stalk form reads dry/warm not knee-grass.
grass._comment_clump_radius_ev3: EV3: R7.1-remainder-2's third round named the untried lever directly -- 'a genuine density lever inside the clumps themselves (more per_clump, smaller clump_radius for tighter packing) rather than further redistributing the same instance count'. 16.0 -> 10.0 packs the same 130 instances into 39% of the area (a squared effect), so each clump reads as a dense patch of continuous cover instead of a loose scatter, with no change to the total prop count or render cost. TUNABLE.
grass._comment_strays: R7.1-remainder round 3: cut from 2000. Round 2's blind critic named the actual problem precisely -- 'near-regular intervals with large uninterrupted gaps... no clustering' -- and 2000 strays spread uniformly across the whole 512m map is a fifth of this layer's instances filling in exactly the gaps between clumps that were supposed to read as clearings. Fewer strays lets the clumps themselves read as denser, clustered patches with real clear ground between them, which is the actual ask (clustering, not raw count).
grass._comment_path_edge_jitter_ev3_remainder_: EV3-remainder-2: see scatter_rules.gd's own comment and bushes' matching entry above -- the village well is where four routes converge, and every ground-cover layer's exclusion edge fans out from it together. TUNABLE.
grass._comment_path_standoff_of12: OF12: replaces path_avoid_radius 6.0, the constant exclusion circle. Holding every tuft exactly 6m off the centreline gave the meadow a ruler-straight inner edge at the same offset on BOTH sides of every path -- which is the 'two nearly straight bands flanking the path' read itself, not a cure for it; five tuning rounds of constant distances (EV3-remainder..-6) never moved that verdict. The standoff now drifts 0.3-7m with ~17m-wavelength position noise, per side of the path independently (scatter_rules.gd::path_standoff_at), so grass crowds the worn edge in one stretch and stands back in the next. min stays near zero on purpose: the path_factor gate already keeps the worn dirt itself clear. TUNABLE.
grass._comment_verge_of12: OF12 round 2: a blind critic on the standoff-only build named the verge beside every path 'the baldest ground in the frame, when it should be the densest' -- with the constant exclusions gone, nothing GREW near the routes either (this stretch of map has almost no grass clumps by seed). The fringe strings extra tufts along the routes by arc length, densest just off the dirt edge, and the standoff noise above culls it stretch by stretch -- see scatter_rules.gd::_place_verge for why that cannot become the planted border again. TUNABLE.
grass._comment_min_height_ev5: EV5: keep out of the pond. Only the pond basin is below -18m anywhere on the map, so a min_height gate is exactly a waterline rule (water level -22.5, terrain_playground.json). Grass wades ankle-deep (0.2m) into the shallows -- was 0.5m, and a blind round read the deeper submerged tufts through the water as 'glass cards', an artifact not a marsh. TUNABLE.
grass._comment_scale: The source tufts are 1.3-1.9m, which is head-high grass. Trimmed to roughly knee height, with a 2.5x spread. R7.1-remainder: raised from 0.26-0.78 (knee height) toward shin-to-hip height, the untried lever the density comment below already named -- bigger tufts at the same count cover more of the near field than more tufts at this size did, without the render-time cost a count increase already proved not worth paying.
grass._comment_colour_jitter: R7.1-remainder round 1's blind critic: 'a single saturated hue with no value range... nothing darker to anchor a black point'. Bigger tufts don't touch that; only colour does. Per-instance MultiMesh colour multiplier, zero extra draw calls or geometry (vegetation.gd).
grass._comment_shadow: No shadow. Thousands of tufts each casting one overlap into a black carpet on terrain that does receive — measured at luminance 0.068 in the near field against 0.27-0.60 across the references. A blade's shadow is not information at this scale.
grass._comment_clearings: Walked straight through, so it cannot hide a creature or block a camera — the arena clearings do not apply. Stripping it left the spawn as forty metres of bare ground in the foreground of every survey frame.
grass._comment_density: Denser than the sparse tufts the critic saw, and pulled back from a first attempt at 21,300. That version took the whole scatter to 28,949 props and the combat survey stopped finishing inside ten minutes — which is a software renderer, so not a frame-rate measurement (D06), but 29k instances is a real cost on the handheld this targets and the coverage was not where it needed to be anyway. Spreading four times the tufts over 512m is not a dense FOREGROUND, it is a thin lawn everywhere. Bigger tufts at moderate count cover more of the near field, which is the half of frame the critic actually measured.
grass._comment_scale_r9_4: R9.4. Was 0.34-1.0. The critic measured the tufts at about 1.2m -- as tall as the well's stone drum -- and said they 'read as pampas, not meadow grass', roughly 2.5x too tall. Same correction as the flowers, and for the same reason: ground cover has to sit under the eyeline or it stops being ground. TUNABLE.
grass._comment_density_r9_4: R9.4. per_clump 70 -> 130 and strays 500 -> 900. Shrinking every tuft to a third of its height frees the screen space that made the old ones read as scenery, and the standing finding from R7.1-remainder-2 is that the field 'reads underpopulated' against the references. Shrink and thicken together, or the fix for one defect deepens the other. TUNABLE.

drygrass._comment: The wispy tufts, warmer and looser, in their own patches. Two grass textures where there was one. The critic counted 2 hue families against the key art board's 6 and said the board's golds appear nowhere below the horizon; this and the flowers are where the warm end comes from.
drygrass._comment_retint: A warm straw modulate over the grass texture. Multiplies, so it stays light.
drygrass._comment_drain_sd16: D41: partial, not total. The green layers give up completely at a station (`drain_suppression` defaults to 1.0) and this dry, wispy, already-half-dead grass mostly hangs on -- so the drained ground is not bald, it changes SPECIES, which is both truer and much easier to read at a distance than an absence.
drygrass._comment_clump_radius_ev3: EV3: same tighter-packing lever as `grass` above, same reasoning -- 19.0 -> 12.0 keeps the instance count fixed and concentrates it. TUNABLE.
drygrass._comment_path_edge_jitter_ev3_remainder_: EV3-remainder-2: see scatter_rules.gd's own comment and bushes' matching entry above -- the village well is where four routes converge, and every ground-cover layer's exclusion edge fans out from it together. TUNABLE.
drygrass._comment_path_standoff_of12: OF12: replaces path_avoid_radius 7.0 -- see grass's matching entry for why a constant radius was itself the flanking-border mechanism. Different wavelength and salt from grass, so the two ground-cover layers do not advance and retreat from the path in lockstep. TUNABLE.
drygrass._comment_verge_of12: OF12 round 2: see grass's matching entry. Dry straw is the scruffy half of a real verge; slightly wider band than grass so the warm tone feathers further out. TUNABLE.
drygrass._comment_min_height_ev5: EV5: keep out of the pond. Only the pond basin is below -18m anywhere on the map, so a min_height gate is exactly a waterline rule (water level -22.5, terrain_playground.json). Dry straw and standing water contradict each other; stays on the bank. TUNABLE.
drygrass._comment_scale: R7.1-remainder: raised alongside grass's own scale bump (same file, same reasoning) so the two layers stay in proportion to each other.
drygrass._comment_scale_r9_4: R9.4. Was 0.32-0.78, cut in proportion with the grass layer above so the two still read as one ground surface rather than two heights of the same plant. TUNABLE.

flowers._comment: Colour accents, clustered hard. Wildflowers grow in patches; spread evenly they read as confetti. Clover is in here because a flower patch with nothing between the blooms reads as pins in a board.
flowers._comment_density: The critic measured saturated non-green pixels below the horizon at 0.000%-0.035% of frame against a design brief that says 'wildflower meadows', and found ZERO in one frame out of 921,600 pixels. A colour accent nobody can see is not an accent.
flowers._comment_path_of12: OF12: this layer's whole path-anchoring stack -- path_bias 0.35, path_bias_per_clump 26, path_bias_side_offset 6.0, path_bias_jitter 4.0, grown one knob per round across EV3-remainder through -4 (the full history is in DONE.md, kept there rather than here) -- is REMOVED, not retuned. Every round treated 'the flowers read as a planted border' as a parameter problem on a mechanism whose only job was to anchor flower clumps to the road, and the owner's verdict never moved: deliberately snapping a garden-accent layer to a path centreline IS planting a border, however jittered. Wildflowers are now ordinary meadow accents that reach a path only when an unbiased clump happens to land near one, gated by the same noise-varying path_standoff as grass (scatter_rules.gd::path_standoff_at) so a chance near-path clump keeps a ragged, per-side-independent edge instead of a matched pair of crescents. max is lower than grass's -- verge wildflowers genuinely hug a worn edge -- and the salt differs so flower gaps do not mirror grass gaps. TUNABLE.
flowers._comment_verge_of12: OF12 round 2: verge wildflowers, the classic path-margin plant. NOT the removed path_bias returning under a new name: path_bias anchored whole 78-instance clump discs to the centreline (a bed), while these are individual draws strung along the arc, thinned by the standoff noise per side, mixed in among the grass fringe. TUNABLE.
flowers._comment_path_edge_jitter_ev3_remainder_: EV3-remainder-2: see scatter_rules.gd's own comment. Distinct from path_bias_jitter above -- that one displaces where a BIASED CLUMP'S CENTRE lands; this one ravels the exclusion edge every instance in every layer is tested against, biased or not. The village well is where all four routes converge, and flowers' own path_bias means more of this layer's instances sit right at that edge than most others.
flowers._comment_min_height_ev5: EV5: keep out of the pond. Only the pond basin is below -18m anywhere on the map, so a min_height gate is exactly a waterline rule (water level -22.5, terrain_playground.json). Flowers reach the waterline and stop. TUNABLE.
flowers._comment_scale_r9_4: R9.4. THE LOUDEST SCALE ERROR IN THE BUILD. Was scale 0.35-0.8 on base_scale 1.0. A blind critic measured the flower heads against the 1.8m NPC standing beside the barn and found them reaching his shoulder, with foreground heads spanning four 0.4m stepping stones -- about 1.8m across on a 2m stem, roughly 4x life size for a meadow wildflower. It is also the second-loudest colour in frame, so the error is maximally visible: the flower layer competes with the buildings instead of reading as ground detail. The key art's flowers are an ankle-height carpet. Cut to a quarter, which puts heads at ankle-to-shin. TUNABLE -- but check any change against a person in frame, not by eye.

rocks._comment: Rocks go where trees will not: they are the layer that makes the steep ground read as stone rather than as grass at an angle. The critic found the previous rocks read as 'dollops of moss' because their lit top face was the same hue as grass — these carry a real rock texture instead of a tinted flat colour.
rocks._comment_slope: The only layer with a MINIMUM slope as well as a maximum, so boulders gather on the shoulders and rises where they belong instead of sitting on flat grass like dropped props.
rocks._comment_drain_sd16: D41: stone does not wither. The drained radius takes the ground cover, not the boulders standing in it -- and a quarry with no rock in it would be a strange quarry.
rocks._comment_min_height_ev5: EV5: keep out of the pond. Only the pond basin is below -18m anywhere on the map, so a min_height gate is exactly a waterline rule (water level -22.5, terrain_playground.json). DEEPER than the waterline on purpose: a boulder breaking the surface near the shore is one of the contact points the water's foam band exists for. TUNABLE.
rocks._comment_align: R9.4-remainder-8-followup: a rock deliberately biased toward slopes but placed world-up, sampled at one centre point, hangs over the downhill side of its own footprint with a visible gap under it -- confirmed in a render, a boulder perched on the hillside behind the farmhouse with daylight showing under its downhill edge. Rocks are rigid, so they should rest flush with the slope; unlike grass/bushes/trees, which stay world-up on purpose (a plant grows against gravity, not perpendicular to the ground it's rooted in).
rocks._comment_harvest_r2_3: R2.3: the world's own scattered rocks, the stone-gathering half of the same fix trees got above. 1-in-14 (0.071) of ~290 rocks is ~21 real gather points.
rocks._comment_tint_r9_4: R9.4. Same treatment, milder, for the same reason: Rocks_Diffuse's faces measure value 0.46 at saturation 0.09, which is a cool light grey sitting on warm ground. The blind critic also noted the rock field is 'one prop instanced rather than a rock field' -- that part is scale_min/scale_max below, not colour. TUNABLE.
rocks._comment_variant_r9_4_remainder_8:
R9.4-remainder-8-rocks-repeat: a blind critic named the rock clusters 'one rock instance duplicated, not a quarry of varied stone' -- same shape, same size, SAME COLOUR, evenly spaced. scale_min/scale_max already vary size (0.28-2.1) and the layer only has 3 boulder meshes to draw from (the fuller Stylized Nature MegaKit that might carry more rock forms is itch.io-blocked, EV1-remainder), so the one remaining honest lever is colour, the same one EV2 used to split one tree mesh into spring/deep/yellow-green variants.
Round 1: three hue-only variants in one narrow value band -- crushed by scene shading, a fresh critic still saw 'no colour/tone variation'.
Round 2: kept hue close but spread VALUE hard (a near-black variant, a near-white one). Real, measured pixel movement, but a fresh critic's own read was sharper than a pass/fail: 'the tonal difference... is lit-face vs shadow-face on the SAME mesh, not a material variant -- rotate the camera and the different rock would go dark too... no true colour/material variety, only lighting-driven contrast.' A pure value swing is genuinely ambiguous with directional-light shading on a faceted low-poly mesh, which already produces its own strong per-face brightness range -- exactly the confound the critic named.
Round 3 changes the axis that lighting can't fake: HUE. A single white directional light changes a Lambertian surface's VALUE with face angle but not its hue, so three genuinely different hue families (warm tan, cool blue-grey slate, rust-brown ironstone) read as different minerals regardless of which face catches the sun -- unlike round 2's same-hue-different-value pair, which a shaded face and a lit face of one rock can produce by themselves. TUNABLE.
rocks._comment_colour_jitter_r9_4_remainder_8: Same mechanism R7.1-remainder used for grass -- per-instance MultiMesh colour multiplier, zero extra draw calls or geometry (vegetation.gd). Pulled back from round 2's 0.22: a wide VALUE-only jitter reinforces exactly the lighting-looking-like-variety confound round 2's critic named, so this now does modest per-instance value spread on top of the three real hue families above rather than trying to carry the whole effect itself. Applies to the pebble meshes too (material PathRocks, untouched by variant_retint above), a second, cheaper source of per-instance variety in the same clump.
rocks._comment_scale_r9_4: R9.4. Was 0.35-1.3, a 3.7x span that still read as one size because most draws land near the middle. Widened to 0.28-2.1 so a clump has boulders AND pebbles in it. TUNABLE.
rocks._comment_anchors_of4_mound: OF4-remainder-mound. Authored outcrops and a talus apron on the ONLY faces of `rises.peaks[0]` the village square and the Rise road can see (the arc from the north-west limb round to the south-west, computed from the two vantage eyes with `tools/_probe_mound.gd`, not guessed). A whole-map placement dump found FOUR rock instances in that entire wedge and none of them on the landform: this layer's own 44-degree ceiling excludes most of a 46m rise's flank, so the layer whose stated job is to make steep ground read as stone was locked out of the steepest ground in the game, and a blind critic read the hill as 'an enlarged pebble' with 'nothing on it, in it, or at the top of it'. Each anchor raises `max_slope_deg` FOR ITS OWN DRAWS ONLY (scatter_rules.gd::_place_anchor) -- the meadow scatter's ceiling is unchanged, so this cannot put boulders on cliffs anywhere else. The `west-spur` pair also absorbs the lone boulder at (80.3,-63.9) that two blind critics independently called 'a stray blob / floating chunk': it is still there, now with company. ALL TUNABLE.
rocks._comment_anchors_of4_mound_r2: Round 2 restructure, and the reason the anchors come in PAIRS. Round 1 gave each site 7-9 boulders in one 1.4-3.2 scale band, and the blind critic's worst-scale-offender finding was the fix itself: 'roughly twenty-five to thirty of them on one hillside... they shrink the hill -- a landform you can count off in five or six boulder-widths from foot to crest is not a landmark... and they are all the same size. No cobbles, no gravel, no single house-sized monolith.' A rock that is a scale REFERENCE has to be either much bigger or much smaller than the thing beside it; a field of same-sized blocks is a ruler with one mark on it. So every site is now a `-block` anchor (one or two large stones) plus a `-rubble` anchor at the same centre and a wider radius (ten-odd cobbles), the big stones weighted toward the FOOT where gravity actually leaves them rather than spread evenly up the face, and `sink` buries a fraction of each so they sit in the ground instead of resting tangent on it. Large stones (scale >= 1.9) went from ~40 to 11.

anchors._why: north-west shoulder, the first stone the square sees -- the block
north-west shoulder -- its rubble
west face bench, roughly half height -- the block
west face bench -- its rubble
south-west face -- the block
south-west face -- its rubble
the low western spur, and the stray boulder's new company -- the block
the low western spur -- its rubble
talus, north-west foot -- the one big stone the tree line stands beside
talus, north-west foot -- graded rubble where slope meets meadow
talus, west foot -- the big stone
talus, west foot -- graded rubble
talus, south-west foot -- the big stone
talus, south-west foot -- graded rubble

OF10-remainder: a cairn at the Rise road's own end (74,-41) -- approach-distance mass for the levelled apron that's there already (`flats._comment_of10_r3`) but reads as too subtle to see from a distance. This layer's own `min_slope_deg` (6.0) exists to keep the meadow scatter off flat grass, which is exactly the ground the apron levels for -- overridden to 0 for these draws only so a deliberately built pile can stand on deliberately flat ground. Offset ~2.5m off the road's own centreline, the opposite shoulder from the trailhead signpost (see paths.trailheads in terrain_playground.json), so the two flank the endpoint rather than sitting on top of each other. The block: two or three stones large enough to read as stacked, not scattered.
OF10-remainder: the cairn's skirt of smaller stones, same centre, wider radius

path_stones._comment: Flat rock plates, scattered thinly on walkable ground. Not a path yet — M7 authors real paths — but a warm grey stone note at ground level, which is a hue the meadow has none of. The critic measured one frame at 0.7% desaturated pixels and observed there is 'no stone, no wood, no built thing, no path anywhere in that frame', where every Palworld reference carries 18-30% desaturated grey.
path_stones._comment_min_height_ev5: EV5: keep out of the pond. Only the pond basin is below -18m anywhere on the map, so a min_height gate is exactly a waterline rule (water level -22.5, terrain_playground.json). The path network ends above the waterline; stray stones stay with it. TUNABLE.
path_stones._comment_paths: The one layer allowed on the dirt paths: stones on a path ARE the path.
path_stones._comment_path_bias_ev3: EV3, found while blind-judging EV4's paths: this layer predated the real paths and its clumps were never anchored to them, so a stone cluster could land several metres of untouched lawn away from the nearest route -- 'a tidy circular stone group... disconnected from the actual path' per the blind critic. path_bias 1.0 snaps every clump centre to the nearest point on `paths.routes` (scatter_rules.gd::_clump_centre); the clump's own clump_radius then spreads instances off that point, so a cluster straddles the road and reads as stones trodden into it rather than scattered independently of it. strays (90) are left unbiased on purpose -- they are the loose stones elsewhere in the meadow, not the path's own texture.
path_stones._comment_clump_radius_ev3_remainder_5: EV3-remainder-5: clump_radius was 8.0, more than twice the path's own visible width (terrain_playground.json paths.width 3.0 + shoulder 1.5 = 4.5m total fade band). A whole-map dump of grandpas-house-route.png's actual region -- the one specific frame two blind critics kept calling a hedge after every ground-cover mechanism (flowers/bushes/grass/drygrass) had already been ruled out by real placement data -- found this layer is the ONLY thing besides grass/flowers there, and split almost perfectly symmetric (7 left / 7 right / 4 on-path of 18 in-frame instances, individual stones up to 7-8m off the path centreline). That is exactly the 'matched clusters... flanking both sides' shape the critics described, on a layer nobody had checked yet. 3.5m keeps the spread inside roughly the path-plus-shoulder-plus-a-verge band instead of forming two crescents on open lawn well past where the path itself has any visual influence.
path_stones._comment_tint_r9_4: R9.4. PathRocks_Diffuse.png is an atlas of pale lavender-grey stones on a dark green ground -- the stone faces measure RGB(132,135,130), value 0.53, saturation 0.04, i.e. a neutral light grey. Rendered over a bright meadow under a strong sun they blew out to RGB(229,230,231) and read, in the survey frames, as scattered paper or marble chips rather than as stones trodden into a path. This is not a bug -- the texture is being drawn faithfully -- it is the wrong value for earth. Warmed and darkened to about the value of the soil they sit in. TUNABLE.

_comment_retint: Mostly EMPTY now, and that is the point. The Kenney kit shipped a bright teal-green palette that had to be remapped wholesale; this pack ships real textures, and `albedo_color` multiplies them, so an unmapped material passes through as authored. Only the deliberate per-layer modulates above apply. A strong colour here would come out as shadow, not as hue.
_comment_retint_bark_ev2: EV2-trunk-colour. Root cause found by rendering the SAME trunk close-up (full texel resolution, no minification) and comparing to the unlit source texture: Bark_NormalTree measures RGB(140,88,67) in the file but rendered at RGB(~217,167,134) in-scene, and Bark_TwistedTree measures RGB(84,76,72) but rendered at RGB(~167,162,153) -- both washed toward the SAME neutral cool tone, and disabling art.json's ambient_light_energy (0 -> still washed toward warm-boosted brown but no longer pale/pink) confirmed ambient_colour (#a8bccc, a cool blue-grey deliberately tuned for GROUND shadow legibility by an earlier fix) is the dominant contributor -- not distance/minification, the item's original guess. Thin curved trunk geometry has proportionally more of its surface at grazing angles to the sun than a flat ground plane, so it draws a larger share of its total light from that cool ambient fill, which a global ambient recolour would fix for bark at the cost of re-breaking the ground legibility fix it exists for. Same lever as the `rocks` layer's own `_comment_tint_r9_4` fix for the identical class of problem (a warm/neutral source washed cool by scene lighting): retint the texture warmer/darker so the SAME lighting pipeline lands on a believable bark colour instead of correcting the light itself. Values solved from the measured gain (rendered/source, per channel) against a target of ~RGB(150,100,70) for normal bark and ~RGB(95,82,72) for the already-greyer twisted bark; verified by re-rendering the same close-up framing after applying.
_comment_collision: Layers marked `collides` get real static collision. Two reasons, and the second is the urgent one: a tree you can walk through reads as a hologram, and — because the camera's SpringArm3D only stops at things with collision — a bush with none lets the camera end up INSIDE it. Two survey frames came back showing nothing but green because the camera was inside a bush during a fight. Grass and flowers must never collide; you walk through those.
_comment_clearings: Open ground kept clear of every layer that can BLOCK. These match the wild creature spawn points in scripts/combat/encounter_director.gd, because a fight starts where a creature is standing and the arena is 11m across: without this, the trees are inside the arena and stand between the camera and the fight. The radius is arena radius plus margin.

clearings._why: the village square and its structures
the practice meadow: the opening's bramblebun and the arena around it

R8.1: the practice trainer's ground north of the square (data/config/trainers.json). Same reason as the entries above -- a trainer battle's arena is 11m across and forms between the player and the creature their opponent just sent out, so without this the fight is watched through a tree. Most of it already falls inside the village square's own 22m clearing; this covers the northern edge that does not.
EV6-remainder: the mill and its crossing -- keeps trees/rocks off the pad and the bridge approaches
EV6-remainder: the ranger station and its yard on the pond route
SC14: the South Bridge and both its abutment aprons -- a tree or a boulder on either rim would stand between the player and the one thing the whole south road exists to show them
clearings._comment_ow5d: OW5D: translated with south_bridge crossings[0] by the same (-5,+1250).
clearings._comment_ow5c_seam: OW5C follow-up: shifted +8 in x with south_bridge crossings[0] (WALL1 seam workaround).

clearings._why: SD16: the Old Quarry's worked floor -- foundations, the conduit head and five rootstone deposits stand on it, and a copse growing through the middle of a working face would undo the read before the drained ground ever got a chance. The `deadfall` anchor above sets `cleared_by_clearings: false` so this does not throw its authored stand away -- see its own note

_comment_footprints: R9.4-remainder-8: unlike clearings above, EVERY layer respects these, including grass/drygrass/flowers -- a footprint is the literal extent of a solid structure, not the wider 'keep the arena/yard readable' radius clearings exist for, so the grass/flowers exemption that avoids a bald ring around the yard has no reason to apply here. Found by real grass tufts standing on Grandpa's own interior floor and rug in a tools/capture_buildings.gd render. Radius is the building's half-diagonal plus a small margin, not a repeat of the wider yard clearing above.

footprints._why: Grandpa's house, 9x7m inside plus walls -- grass was standing on the floor and the rug

the windmill -- at distance sqrt(18^2+14^2)=22.8m from the village-square clearing's own centre, just outside its 22m radius, so the rocks layer (which DOES respect clearings, unlike grass) could still land a boulder against its base. R9.4-remainder-8's survey found one doing exactly that, obscuring village.json's own stated landmark from the meadow view.
the mill -- grass out of the tower and from under the wheel
the footbridge -- grass off the deck and both stone landings
SC14: the South Bridge's deck and both stone landings -- the same treatment the mill's footbridge already gets, at this span's own half-length
